alignments.note: 'to the end that' is the English purpose connector and belongs to the purposive preposition.
The nominalizing article of the purpose infinitive has no separate English word.
The infinitive is rendered by 'should be' around its accusative subject.
The accusative subject of the infinitive becomes the English clause subject.
Anarthrous ἔπαινον is definite by its genitive modifier.
'of' realizes the genitive; the possessive pronoun intervenes.
The appositional substantival article is realized as 'we who'; the nominal 'we' is the head.
'had before hoped' renders the compound perfect participle; 'before' realizes the προ- element.
The article before the name has no English realization.

review_notes: 'to the end that' is the English purpose connector and is kept on εἰς, with the nominalizing article unrepresented; verse 18 compresses the same construction to a bare 'that' and is treated the same way.
The second 'we' resumes the accusative subject through the appositional article τοὺς, so it is not an addition.
